coverage: Origins, unifications, revivals and title identities for the six men’s main-roster championships. This history is not an all-time reign-by-reign or match archive. Historical-title dates may be recognition/taping dates; they do not add non-televised matches to the broadcast archive. The Georgia–National–United States branch is included. Early territorial records can be disputed; the Georgia unification is shown at year precision. This is a researched merger map, not a claim that every historical lineage dispute has been resolved.

wwe.name: WWE Championship
wwe.note: The continuing record behind today’s Undisputed WWE Championship. A new name or belt does not restart its history.
wwe.names: WWWF World Heavyweight → WWF Heavyweight / World Heavyweight → WWF / WWE → Undisputed → WWE World Heavyweight → WWE → Undisputed WWE
wwe.title: wwe-championship

wcw.name: WCW World Championship
wcw.note: WCW’s separately recognized world title. Its NWA heritage does not mean the still-separate NWA championship was retired in 2001.
wcw.names: WCW World Heavyweight → WCW Championship → World Championship (WWF, 2001)
wcw.title: wcw-world-heavyweight-championship

intl.name: WCW International World
intl.note: The record begins with Flair’s NWA title win. After WCW left the NWA in September 1993, WCW continued its own recognition; the International name followed. The NWA record remained separate.
intl.title: wcw-international-world-heavyweight-championship

oldworld.name: World Heavyweight · 2002–2013
oldworld.note: A new WWE title in 2002, with Big Gold heritage. It is neither a continuation of WCW’s record nor the championship introduced in 2023.
oldworld.title: world-heavyweight-championship-2002

universal.name: Universal Championship
universal.note: WWE’s current historical table ends this title with Roman Reigns on April 7, 2024. The 2022 winner-take-all match did not immediately end its separate record.
universal.title: wwe-universal-championship

ic.name: Intercontinental Championship
ic.note: Patterson was the inaugural champion. The Rio tournament and South American title belong to the storyline origin, not a separately documented tournament record.
ic.names: WWF Intercontinental Heavyweight → WWF Intercontinental → WWE Intercontinental
ic.title: intercontinental-championship

us.name: United States Championship
us.note: The Mid-Atlantic/Jim Crockett title continued through WCW and into WWE. Its 2003 return resumed the 1975 record.
us.names: NWA United States (Mid-Atlantic) → WCW United States → WWE United States
us.title: united-states-championship

european.name: European Championship
european.note: Bulldog defeated Owen Hart in Berlin. WWE records February 26; the match aired on Raw on March 3, 1997. Dates here describe title history, not a new broadcast-archive entry.
european.title: wwe-european-championship

hardcore.name: Hardcore Championship
hardcore.note: Introduced by awarding the championship to Mankind; its later 24/7 rule allowed rapid title changes.
hardcore.title: wwf-hardcore-championship

north-american.name: WWF North American
north-american.note: Patterson held this belt when the Intercontinental title was introduced. It continued in Japan afterward, so the origin story is not drawn as a permanent merger.
north-american.title: wwf-north-american-heavyweight-championship

nwa.name: NWA Worlds Heavyweight
nwa.note: Historical background, not an absorbed WWE title. Sources differ on the precise July founding date; the map deliberately uses month-level precision.
nwa.title: nwa-worlds-heavyweight-championship

tag02.name: World Tag Team · 2002 lineage
tag02.note: Today’s RAW title follows the championship introduced on SmackDown in 2002. It does not inherit the older title’s 1971 start date.
tag02.names: WWE Tag Team → Unified WWE Tag Team (shared billing) → WWE Tag Team → Raw Tag Team → World Tag Team
tag02.title: world-tag-team-championship

tag71.name: World Tag Team · 1971–2010
tag71.note: The original WWWF/WWF team title. It kept a separate record during the 2009–2010 unified presentation.
tag71.names: WWWF World Tag Team → WWF Tag Team → WWE / World Tag Team
tag71.title: world-tag-team-championship-1971

wcwtag.name: WCW World Tag Team
wcwtag.note: This is the Mid-Atlantic/Jim Crockett version of the NWA World Tag Team title, later WCW’s. Other regional NWA tag titles are separate records.
wcwtag.names: NWA World Tag Team (Mid-Atlantic) → WCW World Tag Team
wcwtag.title: wcw-world-tag-team-championship

tag16.name: WWE Tag Team · 2016 lineage
tag16.note: A separate championship created for SmackDown. First awarded at Backlash after a tournament.
tag16.names: SmackDown Tag Team → Undisputed WWE Tag Team (shared billing) → WWE Tag Team
tag16.title: wwe-tag-team-championship

world23.name: World Heavyweight · 2023 lineage
world23.note: A new championship announced in April 2023. Rollins defeated AJ Styles at Night of Champions to become its first champion. The 2002–2013 record was not restarted.
world23.title: world-heavyweight-championship

national.name: NWA National Heavyweight Championship
national.first: Disputed: Jack Brisco is documented in October 1980; some histories name Austin Idol earlier that year
national.note: Established in Georgia Championship Wrestling in 1980. Early title histories disagree about the first champion. This branch follows the original 1980–1986 title through its unification into the United States title; the National title was later revived by the NWA in 1997.
national.title: nwa-national-heavyweight-championship

georgia.name: NWA Georgia Heavyweight Championship
georgia.first: Choo-Choo Lynn (1962 sanctioned record; earlier local claims also existed)
georgia.note: The territorial record is traced to Choo-Choo Lynn in 1962, with formal belt presentation in November. Some summaries begin with Sputnik Monroe in 1964. Masked Superstar unified it with the National title in 1981; historical records disagree on the exact date. Later revivals are outside this original branch.
georgia.title: nwa-georgia-heavyweight-championship

events.label: WWE’s separate record begins
events.text: Buddy Rogers becomes the first recognized WWWF champion. NWA history is background; the NWA title was not unified into this championship.

events.label: WCW recognition begins
events.text: Ric Flair is recognized as WCW champion following his win over Sting. This starts WCW’s record alongside its NWA background.

events.label: WCW leaves the NWA
events.text: Flair’s July title win becomes the starting point of WCW’s separate International record after the split.

events.label: Flair unifies WCW’s world titles
events.text: Ric Flair defeats Sting at Clash of the Champions XXVII. The International championship ends; the WCW World record continues.

events.label: Jericho becomes Undisputed Champion
events.text: At Vengeance, Chris Jericho beats The Rock and then Steve Austin. WCW’s title is absorbed; WWE’s 1963 record continues.

events.label: One Undisputed belt
events.text: Triple H receives one belt representing the championship unified the previous December. This is a presentation change, not another lineage.

events.label: A new title, familiar Big Gold
events.text: Eric Bischoff awards Triple H the new World Heavyweight Championship. The belt evokes WCW, but the official reign record starts in 2002.

events.label: Orton unifies the world titles
events.text: Randy Orton defeats John Cena at TLC. The 2002 World Heavyweight record ends; the WWE record continues as WWE World Heavyweight Championship.

events.label: Roman holds both championships
events.text: Roman Reigns defeats Brock Lesnar at WrestleMania 38. Both title records continue under one champion and Undisputed WWE Universal billing.

events.label: A single Undisputed belt
events.text: Triple H presents Roman Reigns with a new belt. The physical redesign is separate from when the Universal record ends.

events.label: Universal record ends
events.text: WWE’s current title history ends the Universal championship with Reigns on this date. WWE’s 1963 lineage continues with Cody Rhodes.

events.label: Patterson’s Intercontinental origin
events.text: The North American/South American unification explains the name in storyline. The North American title actually continued in Japan until 1981.

events.label: Edge unifies U.S. and IC
events.text: Edge defeats Test at Survivor Series. The U.S. championship becomes inactive while the Intercontinental title continues.

events.label: European title absorbed
events.text: Rob Van Dam defeats Jeff Hardy in a Raw ladder match, ending the European championship.

events.label: Hardcore title absorbed
events.text: Rob Van Dam defeats Tommy Dreamer on Raw. The Hardcore championship is retired into the Intercontinental title.

events.label: Intercontinental title deactivated
events.text: Triple H defeats Kane at No Mercy to unify their titles. The IC championship disappears temporarily, returning in 2003.

events.label: Christian wins the revived title
events.text: After its May 5 reinstatement announcement, Christian wins the vacant Intercontinental championship in a Judgment Day battle royal.

events.label: Eddie wins the revived U.S. title
events.text: Eddie Guerrero defeats Chris Benoit in the Vengeance tournament final. WWE resumes the title’s existing lineage.

events.label: Brothers of Destruction hold both
events.text: Undertaker and Kane win both sets at SummerSlam. The titles subsequently separate before the final November unification.

events.label: Dudleys end the WCW tag lineage
events.text: The Dudley Boyz beat the Hardy Boyz in a Survivor Series cage match. WCW’s tag title is retired.

events.label: Four belts, one champion team
events.text: Carlito and Primo defeat The Miz and John Morrison at WrestleMania XXV. Both records continue under Unified WWE Tag Team billing.

events.label: Original World Tag Team record ends
events.text: The Hart Dynasty receive redesigned belts. The 1971 title is retired; the 2002 title continues.

events.label: The RAW tag championship
events.text: The 2002 championship becomes RAW’s counterpart to the newly introduced SmackDown title. The same reign record continues.

events.label: The Usos hold RAW and SmackDown gold
events.text: The Usos beat RK-Bro. Both title records remain active while defended together as the Undisputed WWE Tag Team Championship.

events.label: The two tag titles separate
events.text: At WrestleMania XL, A-Town Down Under take the SmackDown belts and Awesome Truth take the RAW belts. Both existing histories continue.

events.label: RAW title becomes World Tag Team
events.text: Awesome Truth receive the renamed championship. Its lineage still begins in 2002, not 1971.

events.label: SmackDown title becomes WWE Tag Team
events.text: A-Town Down Under receive the renamed belts. This is the continuing 2016 championship.

events.label: Rollins becomes the first champion
events.text: Seth Rollins defeats AJ Styles at Night of Champions. This starts the reign history of a new World Heavyweight championship.

events.label: European championship returns
events.text: Mideon becomes champion after the brief 1999 retirement. The same European title record resumes.

events.label: Georgia title unified into National title
events.text: Masked Superstar defeated Tommy Rich to combine the Georgia and National titles in 1981. Wrestling-Titles records September 12, while The History of WWE lists August 29 and The SmackDown Hotel lists September 19. The tree shows the agreed year rather than a falsely precise day.

events.label: National title unified into United States title
events.text: United States Champion Nikita Koloff defeated National Champion Wahoo McDaniel in Atlanta. The original National title was deactivated, while the United States title continued under Jim Crockett Promotions. The NWA later revived its National title separately in 1997.

world-heavyweight.summary: Established in 2023. The shared name and Big Gold inspiration do not continue the 2002–2013 championship’s official record.

intercontinental.summary: Established in 1979. Absorbed three titles, was briefly unified out of existence itself, then returned with its original record.

united-states.summary: The 1975 Mid-Atlantic title continues through WCW and WWE, including a 2001–2003 interruption.
united-states.title: united-states-championship

world-tag-team.summary: The current World Tag Team title starts in 2002. Earlier tag championships connect through unifications without changing that starting date.
world-tag-team.title: world-tag-team-championship

wwe-tag-team.summary: The current WWE Tag Team title starts in 2016. Its 2022–2024 partnership with RAW’s title did not erase either record.
wwe-tag-team.title: wwe-tag-team-championship

wwe.label: WWWF / WWF / WWE
wwe.text: Established by the World Wide Wrestling Federation (WWWF) in 1963. The promotion became WWF, then WWE; those name changes did not create new championships.

wcw.label: WCW
wcw.text: World Championship Wrestling. Its world title entered the WWF through the 2001 WCW asset acquisition and the December 2001 unification.

intl.label: WCW
intl.text: WCW’s International title, recognized after its 1993 departure from the NWA. The NWA World title remained separate.

oldworld.label: WWE
oldworld.text: Created by WWE in 2002. The Big Gold design echoed WCW, but this was a new WWE championship record.

world23.label: WWE
world23.text: Created by WWE in 2023 as an independent championship.

ic.label: WWF to WWE
ic.text: Created by WWF in 1979. It continued under the WWE company name from 2002.

european.label: WWF to WWE
european.text: Created by WWF in 1997 during its European tour. There was no separate European promotion supplying this championship.

hardcore.label: WWF to WWE
hardcore.text: Created by WWF in 1998 and first awarded to Mankind. This was not an ECW championship.

us.label: JCP / NWA to WCW to WWE
us.text: Created in Jim Crockett Promotions’ Mid-Atlantic territory under NWA sanction. It continued through WCW and then WWF/WWE. NWA is an alliance and sanctioning body, not a synonym for a promotion owned by WWE.

national.label: Georgia / NWA to JCP
national.text: Created in Georgia Championship Wrestling, an NWA territory. It moved into Jim Crockett Promotions and was unified with the U.S. title in 1986.

georgia.label: Georgia Championship Wrestling
georgia.text: An NWA-sanctioned Georgia territorial championship. It joined the National title in 1981, before the National title joined the U.S. title.

tag71.label: WWWF to WWF to WWE
tag71.text: Created by WWWF in 1971; continued under WWF and WWE until retirement in 2010.

wcwtag.label: JCP / NWA to WCW
wcwtag.text: The Mid-Atlantic/Jim Crockett Promotions version of the NWA World Tag Team title became WCW’s tag title, then was unified with WWF’s in 2001.

tag02.label: WWE
tag02.text: Created by WWE in 2002. Later called Raw Tag Team and, since 2024, World Tag Team.

tag16.label: WWE
tag16.text: Created by WWE for SmackDown in 2016. Renamed WWE Tag Team in 2024.

links.label: Unified, Jun 23, 1994
links.text: Ric Flair beat Sting at Clash of the Champions XXVII, ending the International title and leaving one WCW world title.

links.label: Unified, Dec 9, 2001
links.text: Chris Jericho beat The Rock for the WCW title and Steve Austin for the WWF title at Vengeance; the WWF title's record went on as the Undisputed Championship.

links.label: Unified, Dec 15, 2013
links.text: Randy Orton beat John Cena in a TLC match, and the World Heavyweight Championship's record ended.

links.label: Held together from Apr 3, 2022
links.text: Roman Reigns beat Brock Lesnar at WrestleMania 38 and defended both titles as one until WrestleMania XL, where the Universal Championship's own record ended.

links.label: Unified, Nov 18, 2001
links.text: Edge beat Test at Survivor Series to unify the WCW United States title into the Intercontinental title; the U.S. title returned in July 2003.

links.label: Unified, Jul 22, 2002
links.text: Rob Van Dam beat Jeff Hardy in a ladder match on Raw, ending the European Championship.

links.label: Unified, Aug 26, 2002
links.text: Rob Van Dam beat Tommy Dreamer on Raw, ending the Hardcore Championship.

links.label: Unified, Oct 20, 2002
links.text: Triple H beat Kane at No Mercy; the Intercontinental title was inactive until May 2003, when it returned with its original record.

links.label: Followed, Sep 1979
links.text: Pat Patterson, the North American champion, was billed as winning a tournament in Rio de Janeiro to become the first Intercontinental Champion.

links.label: Followed, Jun 1971
links.text: The WWWF's main tag team title passed to its new World Tag Team Championship.

links.label: Unified, Nov 18, 2001
links.text: The Dudley Boyz beat The Hardy Boyz at Survivor Series; the WCW tag title ended and the WWF title went on.

links.label: Unified 2009, retired 2010
links.text: Carlito and Primo unified the two titles at WrestleMania 25; both belts were defended together until the World Tag Team Championship was retired on August 16, 2010.

links.label: Held together, 2022 to 2024
links.text: The Usos won both tag titles on SmackDown and defended them as one until WrestleMania XL split them on April 6, 2024; both records continued.

links.label: Followed, 1996
links.text: WCW's light heavyweight title had been abandoned in 1992; a 1996 tournament crowned the first Cruiserweight Champion.

links.label: Followed, Nov 2001

links.text: Sienna beat Rosemary at Slammiversary XV.

links.label: Followed, Aug 2016
links.text: TNA retired the King of the Mountain title and introduced the Grand Championship in its place.

links.label: Unified, Jun 2018
links.text: Austin Aries, holding both, had the Grand Championship retired into the world title.

links.label: Unified, Mar 13, 2021
links.text: Rich Swann beat Moose at Sacrifice, ending the TNA World Heavyweight title Moose had revived in 2020.

links.label: Followed, Mar 2025
links.text: The International Championship took the retired Digital Media title's place.

links.label: Held together, Jul to Dec 2025
links.text: Kazuchika Okada beat Kenny Omega at All In to hold both as the AEW Unified Championship, until Jon Moxley won the Continental Classic final on December 27, 2025.

links.label: Held together, Apr to Jul 2024
links.text: Bullet Club Gold won both trios titles at Dynasty and held them until they were stripped of the ROH title on July 10, 2024.

links.label: Unified, Aug 12, 2006
links.text: Bryan Danielson beat Nigel McGuinness in Liverpool. The Pure title was revived in 2020.

links.label: Followed, 2021
links.text: ROH replaced the Women of Honor title with the ROH Women's World Championship, first won by Rok-C.

links.label: Unified, Aug 17, 2014
links.text: El Hijo del Fantasma won a ten-way match at Triplemanía XXII and the title became the AAA World Cruiserweight Championship.
